blocks.title: What is this file?
blocks.what: A Service gives a group of Pods one stable name and address. It comes from the core v1 API.
blocks.why: This Service also opens a port on every node, so traffic from outside the cluster can reach the Pods.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because it cannot tell what you want to create.
blocks.comment: What to create: a Service, from the core v1 API

blocks.title: Give it a name
blocks.why: A different name from the web Service lets you try both side by side.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because every object needs a name.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: web-nodeport

blocks.title: Which Pods?
blocks.what: The selector picks every Pod labelled app: web, the Pods from the Deployment lesson.
blocks.why: This is how a Service finds its Pods, whatever its type.
blocks.ifRemoved: The Service has no Pods to send traffic to, so requests fail.
blocks.comment: Send traffic to Pods labelled app: web
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: web-nodeport
spec:
  selector:
    app: web

blocks.title: Which ports?
blocks.what: The Service listens on port 80 and forwards to port 80 on the Pods.
blocks.why: These work as in a ClusterIP Service. The node port comes next.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the Service, because it must say which port to listen on.
blocks.comment: Listen on port 80 and forward to port 80 on the Pods
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: web-nodeport
spec:
  selector:
    app: web
  ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 80
      targetPort: 80

blocks.title: A port on every node
blocks.what: NodePort keeps the cluster address and also opens one port on every node.
blocks.why: Anything that can reach a node can now reach the app, without being inside the cluster.
blocks.ifRemoved: The Service falls back to ClusterIP and works only inside the cluster.
blocks.comment: Also open a port on every node
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: web-nodeport
spec:
  selector:
    app: web
  ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 80
      targetPort: 80
  type: NodePort

blocks.title: Choose the node port
blocks.what: nodePort picks the port number on each node. It must be between 30000 and 32767.
blocks.why: A fixed number is easy to remember and to write down for others.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes picks a free port in the range for you.
blocks.comment: The port to open on each node
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: web-nodeport
spec:
  selector:
    app: web
  ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 80
      targetPort: 80
      nodePort: 30080
  type: NodePort

notes.apiVersion: The API group and version that define this kind. Services are in the core v1 API.
notes.kind: The type of object to create. A Service gives Pods one stable name and address.
notes.metadata: Details that identify the object, such as its name.
notes.spec: The desired state: which Pods to send traffic to, and on which ports.
notes.spec.selector: The labels a Pod must have to receive traffic from this Service.
notes.spec.selector.app: Send traffic to Pods labelled app: web, the Pods from the Deployment lesson.
notes.spec.ports: The ports the Service listens on. Each list item is one port.
notes.spec.ports[].protocol: The network protocol. TCP is the default and suits web traffic.
notes.spec.ports[].port: The port the Service listens on.
notes.spec.ports[].targetPort: The port on the Pods where the Service forwards each request. nginx listens on 80.
notes.metadata.name: The Service name. It must be unique among Services in the namespace.
notes.spec.ports[].nodePort: The port opened on every node, from 30000 to 32767 by default.
notes.spec.type: NodePort opens the same port on every node, as well as a cluster address.

tryIt.result: Starts the two web Pods from the Keep your app running lesson.
TYPE shows NodePort. PORT(S) shows 80:30080/TCP: the Service port, then the node port.

tryIt.command: kubectl run client --rm -i --restart=Never --image=busybox:1.37.0 -- wget -qO- http://<node INTERNAL-IP>:30080
tryIt.result: Prints the nginx welcome page, reached through port 30080 on the node.

check.run: kubectl run client --rm -i --restart=Never --image=busybox:1.37.0 -- wget -qO- http://$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[0].status.addresses[?(@.type=="InternalIP")].address}'):30080

tryIt.result: Removes the Service and the Deployment.

questions.question: Which port do you connect to from outside the cluster?
questions.explain: Outside the cluster, you connect to a node on nodePort 30080. Inside, the Service still listens on 80.

questions.question: Which nodes open port 30080?
answers: Only nodes running a web Pod
questions.explain: A NodePort opens on every node. Each node forwards the traffic to a web Pod.

questions.question: What happens if you delete line 12?
answers: Kubernetes picks a free node port for you
questions.explain: nodePort is optional. Without it, Kubernetes picks a free port between 30000 and 32767.

fix.message: The Service "web-nodeport" is invalid: spec.ports[0].nodePort: Invalid value: 80: provided port is not in the valid range. The range of valid ports is 30000-32767
fix.explain: By default, Kubernetes allows node ports only from 30000 to 32767. Port 80 is outside that range.
fix.fix: Pick a port in the range, such as 30080.
